title: How a Kid From Croatia Ended Up Running Bugatti

scenes.text: A professor in Zagreb reportedly told him that building a car in Croatia was impossible. At twenty-one he started a car company anyway. At thirty-three he became the chief executive of Bugatti. This is the story of Mate Rimac, the boy who was bullied for his accent, and how he ended up running one of the most famous car brands on Earth.
scenes.caption: HOW A KID FROM CROATIA ENDED UP RUNNING BUGATTI

scenes.text: Here is the twist. His company almost did not survive its first big offer. A rich buyer wanted two of his cars, and the only price was moving the company abroad. He said no, lost his only investors, and later called it the best thing he had ever done.
scenes.caption: HE TURNED DOWN HIS ONLY INVESTORS

scenes.text: Every fact in this video comes from published sources, listed in the description. Where sources disagree, we will tell you. And there are a few disagreements, starting with the very first car he ever converted.
scenes.caption: EVERY FACT IS SOURCED

scenes.text: Wikipedia says Mate Rimac was born on the twelfth of February, nineteen eighty-eight, in Livno, which was then part of Bosnia and Herzegovina, inside Yugoslavia. His parents were Zdenka and Ivan Rimac. He was born into a country that, within a few years, would no longer exist.
scenes.caption: BORN 12 FEBRUARY 1988, LIVNO
scenes.chapter: A child who moved to escape a war

scenes.text: Wikipedia says the family moved to Frankfurt, Germany, in nineteen ninety-one, to escape the Yugoslav Wars. They stayed there until two thousand. So a child who would one day run a car company grew up, in his early years, in the country of Mercedes, B M W and Porsche.
scenes.caption: 1991: FAMILY MOVES TO FRANKFURT

scenes.text: In two thousand, the family settled in Samobor, Croatia, where his father founded a real estate company. By our own arithmetic, Mate was about twelve. A new country, a new language at school, and a boy who had spent most of his life somewhere else.
scenes.caption: 2000: SAMOBOR, CROATIA

scenes.text: It was not easy. Wikipedia says he struggled to adapt at school in Croatia and was bullied for his Bosnian accent. So the future chief executive of Bugatti began as a boy who did not fit in. We think that detail matters, because what happened next is a story of a boy proving something.
scenes.caption: BULLIED FOR HIS ACCENT

scenes.text: Wikipedia says a high school teacher, Ivan Vlainić, who later became his mentor, encouraged him to enter a local electronics competition. He won it. He then placed first nationally and represented Croatia internationally. So the first thing Rimac ever won was not a race.
scenes.caption: FIRST WIN: AN ELECTRONICS COMPETITION
scenes.chapter: The teacher, the glove and the mirror

scenes.text: In two thousand five, Wikipedia says he built the iGlove, a glove that could replace the keyboard and the mouse. He was seventeen. The same page says he applied for two international patents at that age, and won awards in South Korea, Germany, Belgium, Switzerland, Malaysia and Croatia, all before turning eighteen.
scenes.caption: THE iGLOVE: A GLOVE INSTEAD OF A MOUSE

scenes.text: He also invented the Active Mirror System, a rear-view system for blind spots. Wikipedia says it won an award at the I E N A trade fair in Nuremberg in two thousand six. So years before he built a single car, a teenager from Samobor was already winning prizes about cars.
scenes.caption: AWARD IN NUREMBERG, 2006

scenes.text: Count the places, by our own arithmetic. South Korea, Germany, Belgium, Switzerland, Malaysia and Croatia. Six countries, before he was old enough to vote in most of them. For a boy who was bullied at school, the world outside Croatia was already cheering him on.
scenes.caption: 6 COUNTRIES BEFORE AGE 18

scenes.text: Now the car. Wikipedia says that in two thousand six, at eighteen, Rimac bought a nineteen eighty-four B M W E thirty three twenty-three i, because it was the cheapest way into racing. He wanted to race. He did not have much money. So he bought an old, inexpensive B M W.
scenes.caption: 2006: A CHEAP 1984 BMW E30

scenes.text: Then the engine exploded during a race. Most people would have bought another engine. Wikipedia says Rimac decided to convert the car to electric power instead, inspired by Nikola Tesla. It is an unusual choice for a teenager with a broken petrol car and not much money.
scenes.caption: THE ENGINE EXPLODED, SO HE WENT ELECTRIC

scenes.text: The sources disagree on the details. Wikipedia's page on Rimac himself says the conversion began when he was nineteen. The page on his company says it was a B M W three series E thirty in two thousand seven, and calls the test car an E thirty M three. We cannot settle that, so we report it as it is.
scenes.caption: SOURCES DISAGREE ON THE DETAILS

scenes.text: What the sources do agree on is the reaction. Wikipedia says other racers mocked the car, calling it a washing machine on the track. An electric car that was slower than the petrol ones, built by a teenager. It looked like the kind of project that fades away after a few races.
scenes.caption: RIVALS CALLED IT A WASHING MACHINE

scenes.text: It did not fade. Wikipedia says that after seven iterations, the car won races and set F I A and Guinness records. The company page lists records from the seventeenth of April, twenty eleven, including a quarter mile in eleven point eight oh eight seconds and zero to one hundred in three point three.
scenes.caption: 7 ITERATIONS, THEN RECORDS

scenes.text: Those figures come with a caution. The company page marks some of the records as pending F I A approval. But the direction is clear. A car called a washing machine became, in the page's words, the fastest-accelerating electric car in its category in twenty eleven. The joke stopped being funny.
scenes.caption: THE JOKE STOPPED BEING FUNNY

scenes.text: Wikipedia says he founded his company in September two thousand nine, at twenty-one. At first it was called V S T Conversions, and it offered electric conversions. The company page says it was founded in Sveta Nedelja, near Zagreb, where suitable facilities were rented.
scenes.caption: FOUNDED AT 21, SEPTEMBER 2009

scenes.text: He was also a student. Wikipedia says he began at VERN University of Applied Science in two thousand seven and earned a bachelor's degree in Entrepreneurial Management in two thousand ten. So during the same years, he was building a company, breaking records, and finishing his studies.
scenes.caption: STUDENT AND FOUNDER AT THE SAME TIME

scenes.text: The company page says early money came from angel investors and from selling patents. And Wikipedia says the company had no employees until two thousand eleven. In other words, for its first two years, the company that would one day make the fastest production cars was essentially one young man.
scenes.caption: NO EMPLOYEES UNTIL 2011

scenes.text: Then came the idea. In twenty ten, Wikipedia says, Rimac met a designer named Adriano Mudri, who was working at General Motors. They started developing a supercar concept at night and on weekends. A supercar, not a conversion. And an electric one, which almost nobody believed in.
scenes.caption: 2010: MEETING ADRIANO MUDRI

scenes.text: The company page says Mudri designed the exterior of the car, and Wikipedia says he is still Director of Design. Rimac's supercar started as a hobby, done in the evenings. That is how a lot of famous companies begin. But very few of them end up owning part of Bugatti.
scenes.caption: A SUPERCAR BUILT AT NIGHT

scenes.text: And he heard the same word again and again. Wikipedia says that a professor at the University of Zagreb reportedly told him building a car in Croatia was impossible. The word on the page is reported, so we do not know exactly how it was said. But the message is clear: nobody expected this to work.
scenes.caption: "IMPOSSIBLE" IN CROATIA

scenes.text: Here is the moment that could have ended everything. Wikipedia says a Middle Eastern royal family expressed interest in buying two cars. But to get that money, Rimac would have had to move the company to the Middle East. He declined.
scenes.caption: AN OFFER FOR TWO CARS

scenes.text: Wikipedia says that refusal cost him his only investors. Imagine that for a moment. A young company with no employees, no factory, no sales, and the only people willing to pay for it are gone. Rimac later called that decision, in the page's words, the best thing he has ever done.
scenes.caption: "THE BEST THING I'VE EVER DONE"

scenes.text: So how did the company eat? The page says it took engineering work for other carmakers, on batteries, powertrains and even whole vehicles. That detail is important. Rimac survived not by selling a supercar, but by selling its brains. The company that made a hypercar began as a supplier.
scenes.caption: SURVIVING AS A SUPPLIER

scenes.text: And the supplier business grew. The company page says Rimac Technology supplies battery systems for the Aston Martin Valkyrie, the Koenigsegg Regera, a Jaguar E-type Zero concept, and a SEAT Cupra e-Racer concept. Wikipedia adds Porsche, Hyundai, Kia, Renault, Jaguar, Aston Martin, SEAT and Pininfarina to the list.
scenes.caption: BATTERIES FOR OTHER CARMAKERS

scenes.text: The first supercar was unveiled at the Frankfurt Motor Show in twenty eleven. The company page calls it the Concept One. Remember where his family lived in the nineteen nineties. A boy from Frankfurt came back to Frankfurt, with an electric supercar, built in Croatia.
scenes.caption: FRANKFURT MOTOR SHOW, 2011

scenes.text: The company page gives the numbers for the production version. One thousand two hundred eighty-seven horsepower, zero to one hundred kilometres per hour in two point six seconds, and a top speed of three hundred fifty-five. A ninety-two kilowatt-hour battery, and about six hundred kilometres of range.
scenes.caption: 1,287 HP · 0–100 IN 2.6 SECONDS

scenes.text: Then comes a surprising detail. The page says the planned production was first stated as eighty-eight cars, and later limited to eight, all sold. By our own arithmetic, that is less than ten percent of the plan. The buyers included a shareholder, Paul Runge, and a company called Applus plus I D I A D A.
scenes.caption: 88 PLANNED, 8 BUILT

scenes.text: Eight cars is not a business. But it was proof. Wikipedia and the company page say that in twenty fifteen, a Rimac Concept One ran at Pikes Peak and finished second, ahead of all the petrol cars. A Croatian electric supercar beat the combustion engines on one of America's most famous hills.
scenes.caption: PIKES PEAK 2015: SECOND PLACE OVERALL

scenes.text: The company page also lists dealers announced at the Geneva Motor Show in twenty seventeen: Manhattan Motorcars, P A C E Germany, and Al Zarooni Group. So a company that once had no employees now had dealers announced in Manhattan, in Germany and with the Al Zarooni Group. Not bad for a project that began in a rented space near Zagreb.
scenes.caption: DEALERS: MANHATTAN, GERMANY, AL ZAROONI

scenes.text: The company page adds more about the Concept One. It lists a curb weight of one thousand eight hundred fifty kilograms, battery cells supplied by Sony, and wheels by H R E Performance Wheels. So a start-up near Zagreb was already buying parts from respected names, and putting them into a car of its own design.
scenes.caption: SONY CELLS · HRE WHEELS

scenes.text: There was also a Concept S, a faster version. The company page lists one thousand three hundred eighty-four horsepower, zero to one hundred in two point five seconds, and a top speed of three hundred sixty-five kilometres per hour. By our arithmetic, that is about ninety-seven horsepower more than the Concept One.
scenes.caption: CONCEPT S: 1,384 HP · 365 KM/H

scenes.text: The big investors followed. The company page says Porsche Engineering acquired ten percent in twenty eighteen. In March twenty twenty-one, Porsche raised its stake from fifteen to twenty-four percent. By our arithmetic, Porsche's holding more than doubled in three years.
scenes.caption: PORSCHE: 10% IN 2018, 24% IN 2021
scenes.chapter: Porsche, Hyundai and Kia come knocking

scenes.text: Hyundai and Kia also joined. The company page says they jointly invested eighty million euros in twenty nineteen, though the TechCrunch article it cites reports ninety million. The two figures may simply be in different currencies, but we cannot confirm that, so we give both.
scenes.caption: HYUNDAI AND KIA: €80 MILLION

scenes.text: Wikipedia also lists Camel Group among the investors. It does not give the amounts for most rounds, and neither will we. What matters is the combination: Porsche, Hyundai, Kia and Camel Group, all betting on a start-up from Croatia.
scenes.caption: A GERMAN, KOREAN AND CHINESE BET

scenes.text: One more number. The company page cites a headline that says Rimac is worth two billion euros. It is a headline, not an audited valuation, and the page gives no valuation in its own text. We repeat it only to show how far a company without employees in twenty eleven had come.
scenes.caption: A HEADLINE: "WORTH €2 BILLION"

scenes.text: The Nevera arrived in this period. Wikipedia says it was shown as the C Two at Geneva in twenty eighteen, and renamed Nevera. The company page lists one thousand nine hundred fourteen horsepower, a top speed of four hundred fifteen, and a production limit of one hundred fifty. A far cry from the eight Concept Ones.
scenes.caption: NEVERA: 150 CARS, 1,914 HP

scenes.text: Then came the biggest twist. Wikipedia says that on the second of November, twenty twenty-one, Rimac was named chief executive of Bugatti Rimac, a partnership between Rimac Group, Bugatti and Porsche. The company page says it was formed on the first of November. The two dates differ by one day.
scenes.caption: 1–2 NOVEMBER 2021: BUGATTI RIMAC

scenes.text: He was thirty-three. By our own arithmetic, he was born in February nineteen eighty-eight, so in November twenty twenty-one he was thirty-three years and nine months old. The man who started a company at twenty-one with no staff was now in charge of a brand that has existed for over a century.
scenes.caption: CEO AT 33

scenes.text: The structure matters. The Bugatti Rimac page says Rimac Group held fifty-five percent and Porsche forty-five. It says Porsche's decision gave Mate Rimac control of Bugatti, and in return Porsche received a larger share of Rimac Group. So the student with the electric B M W ended up leading the company.
scenes.caption: RIMAC GROUP 55% · PORSCHE 45%

scenes.text: Both brands stay separate. The page says Bugatti Automobiles and Rimac Automobili operate as separate brands and manufacturers, with production in Zagreb and Molsheim, France. The company began with four hundred thirty-five staff, about three hundred in Sveta Nedelja and one hundred thirty-five in Molsheim.
scenes.caption: 435 PEOPLE, TWO COUNTRIES

scenes.text: Compare that with today. The company page for Rimac Automobili lists about fifteen hundred employees, though the Rimac biography gives other numbers for earlier years, more than a thousand by twenty twenty and over nine hundred in twenty twenty-one. These are different dates and sources, so we cannot reconcile them exactly.
scenes.caption: FROM ZERO EMPLOYEES TO ~1,500

scenes.text: The first joint car was the Bugatti W sixteen Mistral, presented on the twentieth of August, twenty twenty-two. The name tells you the engine: a W sixteen. Under a chief executive known for electric cars, the first joint car had a petrol engine.
scenes.caption: FIRST JOINT CAR: THE W16 MISTRAL

scenes.text: And Bugatti's next car does not abandon the engine either. Wikipedia says the Tourbillon, unveiled in twenty twenty-four, has a naturally aspirated sixteen-cylinder engine and three electric motors, for one thousand eight hundred metric horsepower. The electric pioneer is building a hybrid with a V sixteen.
scenes.caption: TOURBILLON: V16 + 3 ELECTRIC MOTORS

scenes.text: Automoblog quotes him on the Tourbillon, saying that beauty, performance and luxury formed the blueprint, and that it is more elegant, more emotive and more luxurious than anything before it. He also quotes Ettore Bugatti, whose mantra was, if comparable, it is no longer Bugatti.
scenes.caption: "IF COMPARABLE, IT IS NO LONGER BUGATTI"

scenes.text: The company page also says Rimac entered a technical partnership with Automobili Pininfarina in twenty eighteen. The Pininfarina Battista uses the same architecture and powertrain as the Nevera. So the Croatian company was not only building its own car, but also the electric heart of an Italian one.
scenes.caption: THE BATTISTA SHARES THE NEVERA'S HEART

scenes.text: And it kept expanding. In September twenty twenty-three, the company page says, Rimac opened Rimac Tokyo in Japan and Rimac Katowice in Poland. A company that had no employees until twenty eleven now had branches on opposite sides of the world.
scenes.caption: SEPTEMBER 2023: TOKYO AND KATOWICE

scenes.text: Rimac did not stop at supercars. Wikipedia says that in twenty thirteen he founded Greyp Bikes, a sister company making high-performance electric bicycles. In February twenty twenty-three, Porsche took full ownership, and it is now Porsche eBike Performance. A teenage inventor was still selling companies.
scenes.caption: GREYP BIKES, FOUNDED 2013

scenes.text: And the company page says that in June twenty twenty-four, Rimac announced Verne, an independent brand for robotaxis. They use lidar and computer vision, with no driving input from the passengers. The page says Verne planned to launch five hundred vehicles in Zagreb in twenty twenty-six, and expand to the United Kingdom in twenty twenty-seven.
scenes.caption: VERNE ROBOTAXI: ZAGREB 2026

scenes.text: There is a link back to the Nevera. The company page lists its sensors as eight cameras, a lidar, six radars and twelve ultrasonic sensors. A car that began as an electric supercar for rich drivers also carries the hardware of a car that could, one day, drive itself.
scenes.caption: 8 CAMERAS · LIDAR · 6 RADARS

scenes.text: The honours piled up. Wikipedia lists the Order of Danica Hrvatska in twenty fourteen, bearing the face of Nikola Tesla. Forbes Thirty Under Thirty in twenty seventeen. E Y Entrepreneur of the Year in Croatia, announced in March twenty eighteen. And Motor Trend ranked him ninth on its list of biggest players in the auto industry in twenty nineteen.
scenes.caption: ORDER OF DANICA HRVATSKA · FORBES 30 UNDER 30

scenes.text: In twenty twenty-five, Wikipedia says he was elected to the United States National Academy of Engineering. For a teenager who built a glove and a mirror in Samobor, that is a long way. And note the Tesla connection: the first award has Tesla's face, and Tesla inspired his first electric car.
scenes.caption: 2025: US NATIONAL ACADEMY OF ENGINEERING

scenes.text: On money, Wikipedia cites the Croatian magazine Nedeljnik for an estimated net worth of one point seven four billion euros as of December twenty twenty-five, making him the second richest person in Croatia. It is an estimate by a magazine, not an audited figure, so treat it with care.
scenes.caption: ESTIMATED NET WORTH: €1.74 BILLION

scenes.text: There is one more detail from twenty twenty-six. The Bugatti Rimac page says that on the twenty-fourth of April, twenty twenty-six, Porsche sold its entire stake in Bugatti Rimac, and in Rimac Group, to H O F Capital, a New York venture capital firm. The page lists H O F Capital at forty-five percent of Bugatti Rimac.
scenes.caption: APRIL 2026: PORSCHE SELLS ITS STAKE

scenes.text: That means the story is still changing. The man who turned down his only investors in the early years now sits at a table with new ones. He is also, as of that page, still the chief executive. We will follow the story, and update when the facts move.
scenes.caption: STILL CEO, NEW INVESTORS

scenes.text: So how does a kid from Croatia end up running Bugatti? Look at the pattern in the sources. A boy bullied for his accent, who won an electronics contest. A teenager with patents and awards in six countries. A broken engine that he answered with an electric motor. A refusal that cost him his investors.
scenes.caption: THE PATTERN

scenes.text: And then a company that survived by selling its engineering, built a supercar at night and on weekends, and let Porsche, Hyundai, Kia and Camel invest. Each step looks small. Together, in about twelve years from founding to the Bugatti job, by our own arithmetic, they are enormous.
scenes.caption: 12 YEARS: FROM FOUNDER TO BUGATTI CEO

scenes.text: Which part of Mate Rimac's story surprised you the most? Tell us in the comments. In the other videos of this series, we reveal two things you did not know about the Rimac Nevera, compare it with the Bugatti Tourbillon, and work out what an electric hypercar really costs.
scenes.caption: WHICH PART SURPRISED YOU?

scenes.text: And if you want to spend your money on something you can actually drive every day, our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality for more stories about the cars and trucks people really talk about.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
